### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Most recent/just updated and can't access app

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home, 64-bit  Windows build: 26200  UBR: 9550  WER OS version: 10.0.26200.2.0.0.768.101

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

The new ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop app consistently hangs during startup on my Windows 11 PC. The application remains on the spinning startup screen and Windows subsequently records a `MoAppHang`.

The failure occurs before the normal Codex diagnostics appear to initialize:

- No `.codex\.sandbox\sandbox.log`
- No `.codex\log` output, even with an explicit `log_dir`
- No session transcript created under `.codex\sessions`
- Setting the Windows sandbox to `unelevated` does not resolve the problem
- Disabling the private sandbox desktop does not resolve the problem

Windows Error Reporting consistently records the same hang signature.

## Environment

Windows:

- Windows 11 Home, 64-bit
- Windows build: `26200`
- UBR: `9550`
- WER OS version: `10.0.26200.2.0.0.768.101`

ChatGPT/Codex:

- Package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Package version: `26.924.2738.0`
- Executable: `ChatGPT.exe`
- Executable version reported by WER: `154.0.8037.57`
- Executable path:
  `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\app\ChatGPT.exe`

Hardware:

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080
- AMD Radeon integrated graphics

## Behavior

When launching ChatGPT, the application remains indefinitely on the spinning startup screen.

Windows Error Reporting subsequently records the application as hung.

The issue has reproduced after normal Windows restarts, so forcibly terminating ChatGPT through Task Manager is not required to reproduce the failure.

I also created a separate clean Windows user profile as a control. ChatGPT initially launched successfully there, but that Windows profile subsequently developed the same startup hang.

## Troubleshooting performed

I have tested:

- Windows ChatGPT app Reset
- Complete uninstall/reinstall
- Removal/recreation of `.codex`
- Removal of ChatGPT/OpenAI LocalAppData
- Removal/recreation of per-user MSIX state
- Removal of Codex runtime cache
- Removal of stored Codex Windows credentials
- Fresh Windows user profile
- Normal Windows restart
- Network/DNS/proxy checks
- GPU acceleration disabled
- NVIDIA RTX 5080 explicitly observed as the GPU used by ChatGPT
- Removal of custom MCP configuration
- Reset of transient Codex lock/session directories
- Reset of Codex SQLite state

The problem has continued to reproduce.

## Windows sandbox compatibility tests

Per OpenAI Support instructions, I explicitly configured:

```toml
[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
sandbox_private_desktop = false
```

The application still hangs during startup.

`CODEX_HOME` is not explicitly set, so the default `%USERPROFILE%\.codex` location applies.

The following does not exist after reproducing the failure:

`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\sandbox.log`

In fact, `.codex\.sandbox` itself is not created.

No general `.codex\log` directory was originally created either.

## Explicit log_dir test

Per OpenAI Support instructions, I created:

`C:\Users\Matt\.codex\log`

and explicitly configured:

```toml
log_dir = "C:\\Users\\Matt\\.codex\\log"

[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
sandbox_private_desktop = false
```

The directory exists and is writable.

After restarting Windows and reproducing the startup hang, the directory remained completely empty. No `codex-tui.log` or other Codex plaintext log was created.

This suggests the application is hanging before the normal Codex logging path initializes.

## Windows Error Reporting

The most recent WER report identifies:

- Event type: `MoAppHang`
- Fault bucket: `1864393022899494093`
- Hashed bucket: `0129b23dc445367589dfa7938ba41ccd`
- WER Report ID: `d74d1996-db39-4547-9ac4-18f8fafcfeba`
- WER report identifier: `68ed1af4-a79c-43cc-852a-3ed3369fadd5`

Problem signature:

```text
P1: OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
P2: praid:App
P3: 154.0.8037.57
P4: 6ab1c765
P5: 4e21
P6: 67246080
```

`Report.wer` identifies:

```text
Application Name: praid:App
Application Version: 154.0.8037.57
Hang Signature: 4e21
Hang Type: 67246080
```

Windows displays:

```text
Codex is not responding
```

and the WER report description is:

```text
A problem caused this program to stop interacting with Windows.
```

WER reports `HeapdumpAttached=1`.

Windows also reported generating:

- `minidump.mdmp`
- `memory.hdmp`

for the hang. However, the dump files were removed by WER before I could preserve them. The archived `Report.wer` remains available.

There are multiple archived `Critical_OpenAI.Codex` WER reports from repeated reproductions of the issue.

## Additional WER signatures

The archived report contains:

```text
Additional Hang Signature 1:
4e218a645f7cb06b474ec98544df847b

Additional Hang Signature 2:
ff5d

Additional Hang Signature 3:
ff5d354e1b4cecf65208f29837e972bf

Additional Hang Signature 4:
4e21

Additional Hang Signature 5:
4e218a645f7cb06b474ec98544df847b

Additional Hang Signature 6:
ff5d

Additional Hang Signature 7:
ff5d354e1b4cecf65208f29837e972bf
```

## Expected behavior

ChatGPT should complete initialization and display the main application UI.

If initialization fails, Codex should ideally create enough early-startup logging to identify the component responsible.

## Actual behavior

ChatGPT remains indefinitely on the spinning startup screen. Windows eventually records a `MoAppHang`, while Codex does not create the configured plaintext log, sandbox log, or session transcript.

## Diagnostic artifacts available

I currently have the archived Windows `Report.wer` for the failure.

WER reported generating a minidump and full memory dump, but Windows cleaned those files before I could preserve them.

I can provide the complete `Report.wer` and collect additional Windows diagnostics if needed. I would also be happy to capture another minidump if maintainers can provide instructions for preserving it before WER removes it.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Steps to Reproduce

The issue has reproduced multiple times on the same Windows 11 machine, including after a clean reinstall and across two separate Windows user profiles.

### Primary reproduction

1. Install the current ChatGPT Windows desktop application:
   - Package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
   - Package version: `26.924.2738.0`

2. Launch ChatGPT and sign into a ChatGPT account.

3. Initially, the application may launch and operate normally.

4. Close ChatGPT and/or restart Windows normally.

5. Launch ChatGPT again from the Windows Start menu.

6. ChatGPT opens but remains indefinitely on the spinning startup/loading screen.

7. Waiting does not cause the application to finish loading.

8. Windows subsequently records a `MoAppHang` for the ChatGPT/Codex application.

### Reproduction after clean reinstall

The issue was also reproduced after performing a substantially clean application reset:

1. Uninstall the `OpenAI.Codex` ChatGPT package.

2. Stop the `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` service.

3. Remove the following local application state:
   - `%USERPROFILE%\.codex`
   - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI`
   - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0`
   - `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\codex-runtimes`
   - Stored ChatGPT/Codex Windows Credential Manager entries

4. Restart Windows.

5. Reinstall the current ChatGPT Windows desktop application.

6. Launch ChatGPT and sign in.

7. The freshly installed application can initially load successfully.

8. After subsequent application launches and/or a normal Windows restart, launch ChatGPT again.

9. The application returns to the indefinite spinning startup screen.

10. Windows records another `MoAppHang` with the same repeating hang signature.

### Separate Windows user profile reproduction

To determine whether the issue was caused by corruption in the original Windows user profile:

1. Create a new local Windows user account.

2. Sign into the new Windows account.

3. Launch the already-installed ChatGPT desktop application.

4. Sign into ChatGPT.

5. ChatGPT initially launches successfully in the new Windows profile.

6. Close the application normally and/or restart Windows.

7. Sign back into the new Windows profile.

8. Launch ChatGPT again.

9. The new Windows profile eventually exhibits the same indefinite spinning startup behavior.

This indicates that the problem is not isolated to the original Windows user profile.

### Sandbox compatibility reproduction

The failure also occurs with the documented Windows compatibility settings explicitly enabled.

Configure `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml` with:

```toml
[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
sandbox_private_desktop = false
```

Then:

1. Restart Windows normally.
2. Launch ChatGPT.
3. ChatGPT remains indefinitely on the spinning startup screen.
4. `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox` is not created.
5. `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\sandbox.log` is not created.
6. No session transcript is created under `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions`.

### Explicit logging reproduction

The failure also occurs when a plaintext Codex log directory is explicitly configured.

Create:

`C:\Users\Matt\.codex\log`

Then configure:

```toml
log_dir = "C:\\Users\\Matt\\.codex\\log"

[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
sandbox_private_desktop = false
```

Then:

1. Verify that the configured log directory exists and is writable.
2. Restart Windows normally.
3. Launch ChatGPT.
4. ChatGPT remains indefinitely on the spinning startup screen.
5. The configured log directory remains empty.
6. No `codex-tui.log` or other Codex plaintext log is created.
7. Windows subsequently records another `MoAppHang`.

### Consistent Windows Error Reporting result

Repeated reproductions generate the same WER signature:

```text
Event: MoAppHang
P1: OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
P2: praid:App
P3: 154.0.8037.57
P4: 6ab1c765
P5: 4e21
P6: 67246080
```

The latest archived `Report.wer` also reports:

```text
Application Name: praid:App
Application Version: 154.0.8037.57
Hang Signature: 4e21
Hang Type: 67246080
```

### Important reproduction notes

- Task Manager force-termination is **not required** to reproduce the problem. The issue has reproduced after normal Windows restarts.
- Custom MCP servers are **not required** for the failure to persist. Custom MCP configuration was removed during troubleshooting and the problem continued.
- Switching from the elevated sandbox to `unelevated` does not resolve the issue.
- Setting `sandbox_private_desktop = false` does not resolve the issue.
- Explicitly configuring `log_dir` does not result in an early-startup log being generated.
- A separate Windows user profile eventually developed the same failure.
- Windows consistently identifies the failure as an actual application hang rather than only a visually stuck loading screen.

## Expected Result

ChatGPT completes startup and displays the main application interface.

## Actual Result

ChatGPT remains indefinitely on the spinning startup screen. The application does not initialize its normal Codex diagnostic logging, and Windows eventually records a `MoAppHang`.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0 (build 26A428).

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Not confirmed. TERM is xterm-256color; this does not identify the terminal emulator.

### What issue are you seeing?

Copying response text in the fullscreen TUI is unreliable in my current environment. When text is visibly selected, the footer explicitly advertises:

```text
ctrl+c copy · enter copy & follow · esc clear
```

However, Ctrl+C also participates in interrupting/exiting Codex. When copying appears to do nothing, pressing the same shortcut again can exit the session instead of copying the text.

This makes a normal retry of a harmless operation unexpectedly disruptive. The problem is not just that macOS users expect Cmd+C: the advertised copy shortcut overlaps with session interruption/exit, and the user cannot safely repeat it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The sequence I encounter is:

1. Run Codex CLI 0.157.1 on macOS with the fullscreen transcript UI.
2. Select part of an assistant response. The selection is visible and the footer says `ctrl+c copy`.
3. Try to copy the selected text with Ctrl+C.
4. When there is no apparent successful copy, press Ctrl+C again.
5. The session can exit rather than performing the intended copy.

I have not isolated the exact selection/focus transition or terminal-dependent conditions. Please treat this as an observed interaction problem, not a confirmed diagnosis of the key-routing implementation.

### What is the expected behavior?

Repeating a copy action should not unexpectedly interrupt work or exit the session.

Possible improvements:

- Keep a stable selection/copy state and show clear success or failure feedback, so retrying copy remains safe.
- Separate copying from interrupt/exit actions, or provide a guard against a copy attempt immediately becoming an exit sequence.
- Preserve the normal macOS Cmd+C workflow where terminal support allows it, or offer a clearly documented configurable alternative.

### Additional information

Related reports: #48415, #48122, #48097, and #47996.

Those reports cover the macOS Cmd+C regression. This report emphasizes the accidental-exit hazard of using Ctrl+C as the replacement copy shortcut, especially when a user repeats it because copying appeared to fail.

No claim is made here that the transcript is deleted; the observed problem is unintentionally exiting the active CLI session.

### What issue are you seeing?

After upgrading Codex CLI from `0.156.1` to `0.157.1` under WSL2, Codex no longer starts when `CODEX_HOME` is located on a Windows-mounted drive using WSL DrvFS.

My setup intentionally keeps persistent Codex data on a Windows drive for backup purposes:

```text
$HOME/.codex -> /mnt/e/CodexHome
```

With `0.157.1`, startup attempts to install the new app-server daemon and fails:

```text
Installing daemon from CLI version 0.157.1 into /home/<user>/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon...
Error: Permission denied (os error 13)
To work without the background server, rerun the same command with --no-daemon (including resume or fork and its arguments).
```

The symlink resolves to a DrvFS/9p-mounted Windows drive:

```bash
readlink -f "$HOME/.codex"
```

```text
/mnt/e/CodexHome
```

Relevant filesystem information:

```bash
findmnt -T "$(readlink -f "$HOME/.codex")" -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
```

shows `/mnt/e` as a Windows drive mounted through WSL/DrvFS (`9p`).

This does not appear to be a normal Unix ownership or executable-permission issue:

- all files/directories are owned by the current WSL user;
- `find ~/.codex -not -user "$USER" -ls` returns nothing;
- creating files in the daemon directory works;
- creating symbolic links there works;
- setting the executable bit works;
- executing a shell script stored there works.

The failure appears specifically related to the new daemon installation/runtime mechanism introduced in `0.157.x` interacting with a DrvFS-backed `CODEX_HOME`.

Two controls isolate the problem:

1. Codex `0.157.1` works when `CODEX_HOME` is changed to a directory on the WSL-native Linux filesystem.
2. Codex works with the original DrvFS-backed `CODEX_HOME` again immediately after downgrading to `0.156.1`.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### 1. Put CODEX_HOME on a Windows-mounted WSL drive

For example:

```bash
mkdir -p /mnt/e/CodexHome
ln -s /mnt/e/CodexHome "$HOME/.codex"
```

or otherwise configure `CODEX_HOME` to use a directory under `/mnt/e`.

Confirm:

```bash
readlink -f "$HOME/.codex"
```

Example:

```text
/mnt/e/CodexHome
```

### 2. Install Codex CLI 0.157.1

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.157.1
```

Confirm:

```bash
codex --version
```

### 3. Start Codex

```bash
codex
```

Observed result:

```text
Installing daemon from CLI version 0.157.1 into /home/<user>/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon...
Error: Permission denied (os error 13)
To work without the background server, rerun the same command with --no-daemon (including resume or fork and its arguments).
```

### 4. Verify basic filesystem operations work

For example:

```bash
cat > "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-exec-test" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
echo "execution works"
EOF

chmod +x "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-exec-test"
"$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-exec-test"
rm "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-exec-test"
```

This succeeds:

```text
execution works
```

Symlink creation also succeeds:

```bash
ln -s "dummy-target" "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-link-test"
ls -l "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-link-test"
rm "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/.codex-link-test"
```

### 5. Control: use WSL-native CODEX_HOME

Create a temporary Codex home on the native Linux filesystem:

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/.codex-test-local"
cp "$HOME/.codex/config.toml" "$HOME/.codex-test-local/" 2>/dev/null || true
cp "$HOME/.codex/auth.json" "$HOME/.codex-test-local/" 2>/dev/null || true

CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.codex-test-local" codex
```

With the same Codex `0.157.1` installation, daemon installation/startup succeeds.

### 6. Control: downgrade Codex

Restore the original DrvFS-backed `CODEX_HOME` and downgrade:

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.156.1
codex
```

Codex starts normally again.

This makes the regression reproducible as:

```text
0.156.1 + DrvFS CODEX_HOME  -> works
0.157.1 + DrvFS CODEX_HOME  -> Permission denied during daemon installation
0.157.1 + native Linux CODEX_HOME -> works
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex CLI should continue to support a persistent `CODEX_HOME` located on a Windows-mounted WSL filesystem, as it did with `0.156.1`.

If the new daemon requires filesystem features that DrvFS cannot provide, daemon-specific runtime state should ideally be stored separately on a WSL-native filesystem rather than requiring the entire persistent `CODEX_HOME` to be moved.

For example, persistent configuration, authentication, sessions, and other data could remain under:

```text
/mnt/e/CodexHome
```

while Unix-specific ephemeral/runtime data such as daemon sockets, locks, PID files, staging files, or similar state could use a WSL-native location.

Alternatively, if a DrvFS-backed `CODEX_HOME` is intentionally unsupported with the new daemon, Codex should detect that situation and provide an actionable diagnostic rather than failing with a generic:

```text
Permission denied (os error 13)
```


### Additional information

Keeping `CODEX_HOME` on the Windows-mounted drive is intentional: it allows the persistent Codex state to be included in existing Windows-side backup routines. Moving the complete directory to the WSL-native filesystem would therefore remove useful functionality from this setup.

`codex --no-daemon` appears to be a possible workaround on `0.157.1`, while downgrading to `0.156.1` restores the previous behavior completely.

I searched for existing issues before filing. These appear related but distinct:

- **#31426** — Windows Desktop WSL agent fails when `CODEX_HOME` is on `/mnt/c` because of SQLite/socket runtime state. This is conceptually related because it also concerns Linux-specific runtime state under a DrvFS-backed `CODEX_HOME`, but it concerns Codex Desktop/app-server rather than the new CLI daemon installer.
- **#48043** — Codex CLI `0.157.0` fails to start on native Windows because of a daemon privilege error; `0.156.1` works. This appears to be another `0.157.x` daemon regression, but the error and environment are different.
- **#48161** — daemon executable lookup/startup problems with `0.157.0` under WSL. The reported failure mode is different from the DrvFS installation `Permission denied` described here.

The strongest isolation result is that changing only the backing filesystem of `CODEX_HOME` makes `0.157.1` work, while changing only the Codex version back to `0.156.1` also makes the original setup work.

items.body:
## Environment

- Codex desktop 26.924.22138, build 11645, prod channel.
- Built-in update check reported up_to_date during diagnosis.
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64.
- Timezone: Europe/Warsaw.
- Subscription: not collected.
- Observed/investigated: 2026-09-27.

## Symptoms and reproduction

The user reports that daily historical token usage displays 0 or NaN on days when Codex was actively used.

1. Use Codex desktop for conversations/tasks.
2. Open historical daily token usage.
3. Inspect days with activity.
4. Observe 0 or NaN instead of meaningful usage statistics.

A user-provided screenshot confirms the tooltip “NaN tokena – 23 wrz” (English: “NaN tokens – Sep 23”) in the Polish daily token usage heatmap. The year is not shown in the tooltip. The screenshot was supplied on 2026-09-27. An authenticated usage API response was not captured. This is not yet a deterministic reproduction on a fresh account. This concerns historical statistics, not current quota exhaustion.

## Expected behavior

Display valid daily statistics. If accounting is incomplete, delayed, or unavailable, show an explicit pending/unavailable state. Never render NaN or represent unknown usage as confirmed zero.

## Read-only diagnostic findings

Recent local JSONL transcripts contain token_count events with valid positive numeric total_token_usage and last_token_usage fields. This establishes recorded activity in the sampled sessions, but does not establish exact daily server totals.

The installed frontend uses:

- /wham/usage/daily-token-usage-breakdown for personal history, with start_date, end_date and group_by=day.
- /wham/usage/daily-workspace-user-token-usage-breakdown for workspace history.

The relevant module is webview/assets/queries-87073524ac1e.js inside app.asar.

Potential robustness issue (hypothesis, not confirmed account-specific root cause): the personal selector sums models[].credits without numeric validation or a fallback, equivalent to:

```js
for (const { credits, model } of models ?? []) {
  values[model] = (values[model] ?? 0) + credits;
}
```

Missing credits would produce NaN (0 + undefined), which can propagate through aggregation. Product-surface values are also summed without numeric validation. Please compare the actual endpoint response contract and unit semantics with client assumptions.

The workspace selector fills the requested date range with empty groups/models and zero defaults for missing days/token fields. Missing data for an active day could therefore appear as confirmed zero.

## Investigation limits

- Actual authenticated history responses were not captured.
- The user supplied a screenshot and authorized its publication; uploading the binary image is not supported by the available GitHub connector. The screenshot can be added manually to this issue.
- Zero values are user-reported. NaN is additionally confirmed in the supplied screenshot; the agent could not inspect the live app UI.
- Schema mismatch, missing fields, and delayed/incomplete accounting remain hypotheses.

## Suggested investigation

1. Compare affected responses with expectations for models[].credits, units, product_surface_usage_values and data_freshness_ts.
2. Check whether omitted daily records become misleading zeros.
3. Validate missing/null/non-numeric values and add regression coverage to prevent NaN propagation.
4. Check account/workspace scoping and accounting freshness if the schema is correct.

No credentials, raw transcripts, conversation content, or account/session identifiers are included.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

Locally installed version at reporting time: `codex-cli 0.157.1`. The exact first affected version is unknown; this was noticed with a recent CLI release.

### What subscription do you have?

Not specified.

### Which model were you using?

Not specified; the reported problems concern terminal interaction and first-time login.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS. Local environment at reporting time: macOS 27.0, arm64.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

macOS terminal; exact terminal application/version and any multiplexer are not confirmed.

### Codex doctor report

Not collected.

### What issue are you seeing?

The recent Codex CLI has made basic terminal use on macOS frustrating in two ways:

1. **The usual key mappings have changed.** Basic cut/copy-and-paste is now unintuitive compared with the previous behavior and familiar macOS terminal conventions. Everyday text editing and clipboard operations should not require relearning fundamental shortcuts after an update. The exact affected key combinations have not yet been recorded for this report.
2. **First-time CLI login is broken in the reported experience.** The login link shown in the terminal is not clickable, and the CLI does not automatically open the default browser (Safari or Chrome). This leaves the normal first-login flow without a usable browser handoff, while the clipboard behavior also makes handling the link unnecessarily awkward.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reported workflow (not independently reproduced while filing):

1. Launch a recent Codex CLI release in a terminal on macOS.
2. Try the usual text-editing and cut/copy-and-paste workflow; observe that the key mappings no longer behave as expected from previous use.
3. On first launch without an existing login, start the CLI sign-in flow.
4. Observe that Safari/Chrome does not open automatically.
5. Try opening the displayed login link from the terminal; the link is not clickable.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Preserve familiar macOS terminal keyboard and clipboard behavior. If key mapping changes are intentional, provide clear guidance and an easy way to restore the previous mappings.
- Open the system default browser automatically for browser-based login.
- Provide a usable, clickable login URL where supported, plus clear manual instructions and a URL that can be easily selected/copied if automatic browser launch fails.

### Additional information

Related reports for the keyboard/clipboard portion:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48415
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47996

This report also captures the first-login browser/link failure. It is not yet known whether the two symptoms share a cause. No authentication URLs, credentials, or tokens are included.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1

### What subscription do you have?

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6-Astra

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

In normal daemon mode, Codex CLI displays a Git-parent trust warning for an empty non-Git folder. The current directory and alleged repository root identify the same Windows directory, differing only in letter case. This is misleading at a security-sensitive consent boundary.

> Note: This was tested both elevated and non-elevated. A detailed example is shown but can also be easily reproduced by simply opening PowerShell (5.1/7.x) and typing codex. The message appears even when the current directory is the users home directory, which has no git.

## Environment

- Windows, unelevated PowerShell process (token checked).
- Tested executable: `C:\Users\user01\AppData\Local\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe`
- CLI version: `codex-cli 0.157.1`.
- Test folder: `C:\Users\user01\AppData\Local\Temp\CodexTrustRepro-20260927\plain`.
- No `.git` or `.lore` markers found in the test folder or any ancestor through `C:\`.
- No Unreal process or project content is required for this reproduction.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Reproduction

Use a new, untrusted directory outside any repository. Run from ordinary PowerShell:

```powershell
$testFolder = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ('CodexTrustRepro-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') + '\plain')
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $testFolder | Out-Null
$cliPath = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe'
& $cliPath --no-alt-screen -C $testFolder
```

Inspect the folder-trust screen without accepting trust. Escape returns to Agent Command Center; Ctrl+C exits the client. Do not stop the shared daemon.

Repeat against the SAME untrusted folder:

```powershell
& $cliPath --no-daemon --no-alt-screen -C $testFolder
& $cliPath --no-alt-screen -C $testFolder.ToLowerInvariant()
```

Dismiss each prompt before starting the next comparison. The lowercase-path comparison is for a conventional case-insensitive Windows folder; it is diagnostic, not a proposed general-purpose path conversion.

## Observed results

| Invocation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Normal daemon mode, mixed-case path | Incorrect Git-subdirectory warning |
| `--no-daemon`, mixed-case path | Folder-only trust prompt, no Git warning |
| Normal daemon mode, lowercase path | Folder-only trust prompt, no Git warning |

Normal mode displayed:

```text
Folder access
C:\Users\user01\AppData\Local\Temp\CodexTrustRepro-20260927\plain

Note: You’re in a subdirectory of a Git project. Trusting will apply to the
repository root:
c:\users\user01\appdata\local\temp\codextrustrepro-20260927\plain
```

All three cases still asked the user whether to trust the folder. No prompt was accepted and no model task was submitted.

The user configuration SHA-256 was identical before and after the two daemon-mode comparisons.
No trust entry containing `codextrustrepro` was present afterward. The hash baseline was taken after the initial no-daemon test, not before the entire investigation.

### What is the expected behavior?

## Expected behavior

- Display the actual trust target accurately.
- Do not describe equivalent Windows paths as a parent/child relationship merely because their casing differs.
- Mention Git only when Git repository discovery actually establishes a repository.
- If trust truly applies to a parent, display that distinct parent explicitly.
- Keep user consent; do not suppress the trust prompt to fix its wording.

## Interpretation and limits

The results strongly suggest a case-normalization mismatch between the client and shared-daemon trust metadata. This is a hypothesis, not a source-code-confirmed root cause. The incorrect Git label may be a separate overly broad UI condition.

These tests demonstrate incorrect wording. They do not demonstrate unintended parent-directory trust: no trust was accepted, and the displayed paths referred to the same directory.

### Additional information

Reproduces on this Windows system with Codex CLI 0.157.1 in shared-daemon mode, including in an empty non-Git directory. Independent confirmation on another Windows system is requested.

### What issue are you seeing?

In ChatGPT Desktop on macOS, **Settings → Environments** still shows multiple stale Cloud Environment entries (for example: LG DEV, SPYDROID, BMW, SCAN, and other old entries).

The same stale environments **do not appear on the web** at:

`https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/environments`

The backend also returns only one active environment, **NetScope**, from both:

`GET /backend-api/wham/environments`

and

`GET /backend-api/wham/environments/search?limit=100`

So this appears to be a **desktop-only stale UI/state synchronization issue**.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open ChatGPT Desktop on macOS.
2. Go to **Settings → Environments**.
3. Observe stale environment entries that were created previously on this Mac.
4. Open the same settings page on the web.
5. Observe that the web view shows only the currently active environment.
6. Restart ChatGPT Desktop.
7. The stale desktop-only entries remain visible.

### Troubleshooting already completed

- Confirmed ChatGPT Desktop is on the latest available build: `26.924.22138`.
- Confirmed Desktop and Codex CLI use the same ChatGPT account.
- Verified both environment backend endpoints return only **NetScope**.
- Cleared local Codex project/environment registry state.
- Verified local ChatGPT/Codex project registry count is `0`.
- Verified local environment map count is `0`.
- Removed stale local `environment.toml` files after backing them up.
- Cleared ChatGPT Desktop UI/cache storage after backing it up.
- Restarted the app after cleanup.
- Verified the stale names no longer exist in active local project/environment records.
- Conversations/chats were intentionally left untouched.

Despite all of the above, the stale environments are still displayed in the macOS Desktop UI.

### Expected behavior

The macOS desktop **Settings → Environments** list should match the current account/backend state and the web UI.

If an environment no longer exists in `/backend-api/wham/environments*`, it should not continue to appear as an editable stale entry in Desktop.

The app should either:
- automatically purge stale environment UI records, or
- offer a safe refresh/reset action that does not delete conversations.

### Feedback/session ID

`no-active-thread-01a0e4b8-4c40-7ea2-ab33-7f00de155493`

Issue reproduced on Sep 27, 2026 around 22:30–23:15 CEST.

The feedback submission included ChatGPT diagnostic logs and browser logs.

### Additional information

The stale entries are **desktop-only**. The web UI and backend environment endpoints are already clean and show only `NetScope`.

Please keep existing conversations intact; deleting chats is not required to reproduce or troubleshoot this issue.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.157.1`

The issue started immediately after updating from `0.156.1` to `0.157.1` using the Windows installer:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c '$env:CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1; irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex'
```

### Platform

Windows x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

While using the Codex TUI, large amounts of raw terminal/control-sequence-looking text are suddenly inserted into the composer by themselves. Once it starts, the input rapidly fills with sequences and is effectively unusable.

This is not intentional keyboard input and can happen randomly during normal use.

A screenshot showed the composer filled with repeated encoded-looking fragments/control sequences.

### Regression

This appears to be a regression in `0.157.1`.

I installed `0.156.1` again and explicitly launched that version. The problem stopped occurring after the downgrade.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows x64, update Codex CLI from `0.156.1` to `0.157.1`.
2. Start Codex normally.
3. Use the TUI for a while.
4. Raw terminal/control sequences may suddenly begin being inserted into the prompt continuously.
5. Downgrade to `0.156.1`.
6. The issue no longer occurs.

### Expected behavior

Terminal keyboard/control sequences should be interpreted by the TUI and should never appear as literal/random text in the composer.

### Additional information

There are two Codex installations on the machine:
- Standalone installer: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe`
- npm installation: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\codex.cmd`

The standalone installer was the `0.157.1` binary exhibiting the issue. The npm-installed `0.156.1` binary works normally.

Possibly related to #48680, but in this case the sequences appear randomly/continuously rather than only from a known custom Shift+Enter mapping.

items.body:
### Extension version

`26.917.62051`

### Subscription

ChatGPT Plus

### IDE

Visual Studio Code `1.138.0`

Commit:

`7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda`

Architecture:

`x64`

### Primary environment

- LMDE 6 (Faye)
- Debian 12 / Bookworm based
- Linux kernel `6.1.0-53-amd64`
- x86_64

The same issue is also reproducible on a separate Windows machine using a different ChatGPT Plus account.

### Description

Rate-limit and usage information is no longer available anywhere in the Codex VS Code extension.

This affects all locations where usage information was previously available:

- `/status`
- `Settings → Usage`
- `Work locally`

Running `/status` currently shows:

```text
Status

Session/Thread:
[redacted]

Context:
84% left (40,751 used / 258K)

Rate limit:
Unavailable
```

Context-window usage continues to work correctly, while account usage and rate-limit information are unavailable.

The issue is reproducible on two independent environments:

- LMDE 6 / Linux
- Windows on a separate machine

The two environments use separate ChatGPT Plus accounts.

The issue was first noticed around September 24–25, 2026. The Codex extension had been automatically updated shortly before the usage information disappeared.

Before the update, usage and rate-limit information were displayed normally.

Because the same behavior occurs across different machines, operating systems, and ChatGPT Plus accounts, it does not appear to be specific to a single local configuration or account.

This appears to be a regression in the VS Code extension.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Codex VS Code extension version `26.917.62051`.
2. Sign in with a ChatGPT Plus account.
3. Open Codex in VS Code.
4. Run `/status`.
5. Observe that context-window usage is displayed normally.
6. Observe that the rate-limit section displays:

```text
Rate limit:
Unavailable
```

7. Open `Settings → Usage`.
8. Observe that usage information is unavailable.
9. Open the `Work locally` menu.
10. Observe that the remaining-usage information is also unavailable.

### Actual behavior

The extension does not expose account usage or rate-limit information through any of the available UI surfaces.

`/status` reports:

```text
Rate limit:
Unavailable
```

The same information is also missing from `Settings → Usage` and `Work locally`.

### Expected behavior

The extension should display the current account usage and rate-limit information as it did before the update.

Usage information should remain available through:

- `/status`
- `Settings → Usage`
- `Work locally`

This should include the applicable remaining usage and reset information.

### Reproducibility

The issue has been reproduced across independent environments:

- Linux / LMDE 6 x86_64
- Windows
- separate machines
- separate ChatGPT Plus accounts

The behavior is consistent across both environments.

### Additional context

The issue was first noticed around September 24–25, 2026, shortly after an automatic Codex extension update.

The standalone Codex CLI is not installed on the primary Linux environment, so no standalone CLI comparison is available.

Context-window usage continues to be reported correctly while account usage/rate-limit information is unavailable. This suggests that the issue is limited to the usage/rate-limit reporting functionality rather than the entire `/status` command.

Session/thread identifiers and other account-specific information have been intentionally redacted from this public report.

I’m aware this may overlap with other recent reports about unavailable usage/rate-limit information. I’m providing this report as an additional reproducible case across Linux and Windows environments.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (codex-cli 0.157.1, Linux)

### What feature would you like to see?

Make the PageUp/PageDown scroll step in the fullscreen transcript (now the default since #47178) configurable, e.g. by honouring the existing `[tui.keymap.pager]` `half_page_up` / `half_page_down` / `page_up` / `page_down` bindings in the main view.

Currently the main fullscreen view hardcodes a full-screen step for unmodified PageUp/PageDown in `TranscriptView::handle_scroll_key` (`codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_view/input.rs`):

```rust
(KeyCode::PageUp, KeyModifiers::NONE) => {
    self.scroll(cells, -(self.area.height.saturating_sub(1).max(1) as isize));
}
```

The configurable pager keymap is only consulted via `TranscriptView::navigate_pager`, which is used by the Ctrl+T overlay and the backtrack preview, not by the main view. So there is no way to get half-page scrolling in the default fullscreen UI. Before fullscreen became the default, users could get it from their terminal's scrollback (e.g. a terminal half-page scroll binding).

Suggested behaviour: route main-view PageUp/PageDown (and any other keys bound to pager scroll actions) through the pager keymap, so that e.g.

```toml
[tui.keymap.pager]
page_up = []
page_down = []
half_page_up = "page-up"
half_page_down = "page-down"
```

applies to the fullscreen transcript as well. Defaults would stay unchanged.

### Additional information

Workaround for now: `[tui] fullscreen_transcript = false` plus terminal-side scrolling, which gives up fullscreen search and selection.

items.body:
### Summary

On Codex CLI **0.157.1** under **WSL2 / Ubuntu 24.04**, the TUI has become unreliable in a way that did not occur in my earlier Codex versions.

Two symptoms appear together:

1. **Selecting/highlighting text with the mouse can freeze or crash the TUI.**
2. After a freeze/restart, the same conversation can remain locked as **"This conversation is open in another app"**, even though the visible TUI is gone. Long-running child jobs may continue in the background while the UI is frozen.

This makes long-running engineering/training sessions difficult to recover safely.

### Environment

- Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.157.1`
- Platform: WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04.x, x86_64
- Host: Windows desktop
- Launch command used during recovery attempts:
  ```bash
  codex -c tui.whimsy=false resume --last
  ```
- The issue still occurred with `tui.whimsy=false`.

### Reproduction / observed sequence

1. Start or resume a long-running Codex TUI session.
2. The session launches child tooling/training processes normally.
3. Use the mouse to select/highlight text in the TUI.
4. The Codex screen freezes or becomes unresponsive.
5. In another shell, the Codex process tree is still alive.
6. In at least one occurrence, a Python child job continued running even though the TUI appeared frozen:
   ```text
   codex
    ├─ codex-code-mode-host
    └─ python -u scripts/train_privileged_bc.py ...
   ```
7. After the Python child completed, the TUI still did not recover. Process inspection then showed only Codex/helper processes remaining, with no active training child.
8. Killing/restarting Codex and running `codex resume --last` could then show:
   ```text
   This conversation is open in another app
   Close it there and press R to continue here.
   ```
   even though there was no usable second window/session to close.
9. Recovery required manually terminating stale Codex app-server/code-mode-host processes, then resuming the session again.

### Process evidence from one occurrence

While the TUI appeared frozen:

```text
PID      STAT  %CPU  ELAPSED  CMD
604154   Sl+    0.9  40:10    codex -c tui.whimsy=false resume --last
626245   Sl     0.1   06:46   codex-code-mode-host
```

A process-tree check showed an active child:

```text
python -u scripts/train_privileged_bc.py ...
```

Later, after that child finished, the Codex TUI remained stuck and no training Python process remained.

### Expected behavior

- Mouse selection/highlighting should not freeze or crash the Codex TUI.
- If the renderer/TUI dies or becomes disconnected, child jobs may continue if that is intentional, but the conversation ownership state should remain recoverable.
- A stale/dead TUI should not indefinitely hold the conversation writer lock.
- `codex resume --last` should either recover the existing session or provide a supported takeover/release mechanism.

### Actual behavior

- Mouse selection can make the TUI unusable.
- Backend/child work can continue independently of the frozen UI.
- After recovery attempts, stale conversation ownership can block resume with "open in another app".
- Manual process inspection and `kill`/`pkill` are required to recover.

### Regression

This has been happening frequently only in recent Codex versions. The same workflow was previously stable for me.

### Related issues

This appears related to, but more severe than:

- #48233 — selection/highlighting latency in 0.157.0
- #48226 — resumed TUI stops processing input while holding writer lock
- #41849 / #44063 — stale writer ownership after client disconnects

The distinctive behavior here is the combination of **mouse-selection-triggered TUI freeze on 0.157.1**, **background child job continuation**, and **stale conversation ownership during recovery**.

I can provide additional sanitized process trees / screenshots if useful.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.157.1`

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### Which model were you using?

Not recorded; this report concerns terminal selection and clipboard behavior.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.7 (build 25G229).

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

Orca 1.4.215, using its embedded terminal to run a Codex CLI session.

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating Codex CLI, ordinary mouse drag selection in a session no longer triggers Orca's copy-on-select behavior. This worked before the update; the last working Codex version is not known.

Orca's **Copy on Select** setting has remained enabled throughout. Pressing **Command+C** after an ordinary drag selection also does not copy the intended text.

Holding **Option** while dragging does successfully select, automatically copy, and allow the text to be pasted elsewhere. This workaround was verified by the affected user, including the paste result, not just the selection highlight.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On macOS, enable **Settings → Terminal → Terminal Interaction → Copy on Select** in Orca.
2. Run Codex CLI 0.157.1 in an Orca terminal session and obtain some transcript output.
3. Drag over transcript text without holding a modifier, release, and attempt to paste elsewhere. The intended text is not copied.
4. Try Command+C after ordinary drag selection. The intended text is still not copied.
5. Hold Option while dragging over the same text, release, and paste elsewhere. The selected text is copied automatically and pastes successfully.

### What is the expected behavior?

The terminal's configured ordinary drag-to-copy behavior should continue working after a Codex update, or Codex should provide a supported way to preserve native terminal selection and copy-on-select.

### Additional information

Inspection of the installed Orca assets confirms that its terminal uses `macOptionClickForcesSelection: true`, and its copy-on-select handler depends on the terminal's selection-change event and an actual terminal selection.

The observed difference between ordinary and Option-assisted selection is consistent with Codex handling mouse selection internally instead of allowing Orca's native selection handler to run. This is a hypothesis; the precise Codex change responsible has not been verified.

Related:
- #47996: Command+C copying regression in iTerm2 on macOS.
- #48664: Request to disable mouse capture independently of alternate-screen mode.

This report adds a macOS/Orca copy-on-select reproduction and a verified Option-drag workaround. No downgrade, `--no-alt-screen`, or configuration workaround has been tested for this report.

items.body:
### What happened

`codex` fails to start because the managed app-server daemon cannot be installed:

```
Installing daemon from CLI version 0.157.1 into %USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages/app-server-daemon...
Error: Access is denied. (os error 5)
To work without the background server, rerun the same command with --no-daemon (including resume or fork and its arguments).
```

The install leaves a consistent half-finished state behind, which is the useful clue:

```
%USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases      <- empty directory
%USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\install.lock  <- 0 bytes
```

So directory creation and lock-file creation both **succeed**. The failure happens after that, and it is not a plain permission problem.

### Root cause

`prepare_install_windows.rs` (`select_release`) does not create the `current` junction directly. On the cold path it creates a temp dir, creates a **real directory** named `current` inside it, then converts that existing directory into a mount-point junction via `DeviceIoControl(..., FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT, ...)`, and finally renames it into place.

That conversion is what returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`. Creating a *new* junction on the same machine, in the same directory, works fine:

```powershell
# both succeed, in .codex\packages and in %TEMP%
mklink /J link target
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path link -Target target
```

Only the "open an existing directory with `GENERIC_WRITE` + `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` and set a reparse point on it" path is blocked. On this machine `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` is running, and a filter driver blocking reparse-point writes (a standard junction-escape mitigation) would produce exactly this. If that is Codex's own sandbox driver, Codex is blocking its own daemon install.

### Reproduction

```powershell
Remove-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon" -Recurse -Force
codex app-server daemon start   # -> Error: Access is denied. (os error 5)
```

`codex app-server daemon start` reproduces this without a tty, which is much easier to automate than the TUI path (the TUI exits with `stdin is not a terminal` *before* reaching the install step).

### Ruled out

Each of these was tested and eliminated, so please don't re-litigate them:

| Hypothesis | Evidence against |
|---|---|
| File lock / stale `install.lock` | `install.lock` opens exclusively; no process holds it |
| Missing write permission | Manually copying the 322 MB `codex.exe` into the target path succeeds |
| ACL on `.codex` | The explicit `CodexSandboxUsers: ReadAndExecute` ACE looks guilty but isn't — the user has FullControl at every level, and that group only contains the two Codex sandbox accounts |
| Directory location | Pointing `CODEX_HOME` at a brand-new `%TEMP%` dir fails identically |
| Insufficient privilege | Codex *refuses* to run elevated: "start the Windows daemon from a non-elevated terminal" |
| Antivirus | Defender service not running (`Get-MpPreference` returns 0x800106ba) |
| Job Object (#44503) | Launching via WMI to escape the job gives the same os error 5; a real job problem reports a different, explicit error |
| Version regression (#48043) | **0.156.1 fails identically.** Downgrading does not help here, so this is a distinct bug from #48043 |
| Disk space | 19.4 GiB free |

`RUST_LOG=trace` only yields a backtrace with all-`<unknown>` symbols, which is why the source reading was necessary.

### Workaround

Building the layout by hand makes the installer take the warm path and skip the conversion entirely. The daemon then starts and runs normally:

```powershell
$root = "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon"
$src  = "<npm global>\@openai\codex\node_modules\@openai\codex-win32-x64\vendor\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\codex.exe"
$rel  = "$root\releases\0.157.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$rel\bin"
Copy-Item $src "$rel\bin\codex.exe" -Force
cmd /c "mklink /J `"$root\current`" `"$rel`""
codex app-server daemon start
```

Result:

```json
{"status":"running","backend":"pid","managedCodexVersion":"0.157.1","cliVersion":"0.157.1","appServerVersion":"0.157.1"}
```

`codex doctor` then reports `✓ app-server running`. The layout contract came from `managed_install.rs`: `current\bin\codex.exe` (packaged) with `current\codex.exe` as the legacy fallback, and the release directory must be `<three-part version>-<target triple>`.

This has to be redone after every CLI upgrade, since a version mismatch triggers the updater and walks back into the same code path.

### Suggested fix

Treat the reparse-point conversion as best-effort: if `FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT` fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, fall back to creating the junction directly (which works even when converting does not), or fall back to a plain directory / the legacy standalone layout instead of failing the whole install. An unavailable junction should degrade to ephemeral mode rather than block startup.

### Environment

- Windows 10 Pro/Home 10.0.19045 x64
- codex-cli 0.157.1 (also reproduced on 0.156.1), npm global install
- Terminal: VS Code integrated terminal, non-elevated
- `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"` in config.toml; `codex doctor` reports sandbox provisioning complete and 0 failures
- `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` running

Related but distinct: #48043 (same subsystem, but downgrading fixes that one and not this), #44503 (Job Object check, different error message).

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex CLI/TUI 0.157.1 on Linux, with multiple TUIs attached to a shared local app-server daemon.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please expose a **supported, client-scoped notification or query for the thread currently displayed by a particular TUI**. A terminal integration needs the complete native thread ID that this client is showing so it can persist an exact `codex resume <thread-id>` target for that terminal pane. A list of loaded threads or the thread that most recently received a turn does not establish the user's current display selection.

A TUI-local `displayed-thread-changed` event is one possible design; a documented app-server interface is also fine if it explicitly associates a client instance with its selected thread. The signal needs a verifiable client/pane origin (for example, delivery from the TUI process) and the full resumable thread ID. It should report initial selection, new/resume/fork, a switch to an already loaded thread and the switch back, including before another prompt. Background or subagent activity must not change the selection unless the user actually displays that thread. Client-generation and ordering information, or an equivalent guarantee, should prevent a delayed report from a previous TUI instance overwriting the current choice.

### Additional information

Our use case is persistent terminal panes with one Codex TUI each. Several TUIs may share a local daemon and may use the same working directory. After restart, the terminal manager must resume the exact conversation that was last visible in *each* pane. `cwd`, recency, loaded-thread lists and background turn activity cannot safely identify that conversation or its client.

We also reproduced the first-client daemon environment problem: a hook for pane B had B's correct `session_id` but inherited pane A's terminal identity. That bug is already tracked in #48500, and #44902 discusses forwarding triggering-client context to lifecycle hooks; #48778 covers broader daemon-environment inheritance. **This issue is scoped to display selection after startup.** Fixing hook provenance alone would still leave no documented way to observe a local switch X → Y → X between already loaded threads when no lifecycle hook or new prompt is guaranteed. Conversely, a client-local display event could provide both the selected ID and its terminal provenance without treating daemon process environment as client identity.

The [TUI source already has `current_displayed_thread_id()`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.1/codex-rs/tui/src/app/thread_routing.rs#L190-L201), described as the thread whose transcript is currently on screen. The [documented `SessionStart` hook](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#sessionstart) covers lifecycle sources (`startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`), not every display change. We could not find a documented client-scoped display-selection event for external integrations.

**Acceptance example:** Attach two TUIs in different panes (even with the same `cwd`) to one daemon. In pane A, display already loaded thread X, switch to Y and back to X while pane B remains on Z; also start a background thread. An external integration should observe A:X → A:Y → A:X and B:Z, without attributing any A event to B or treating the background thread as selected. After restarting A's TUI, its initial selection should be reportable again. The integration can then persist the exact last visible native ID for each pane without inspecting screen text or guessing from daemon activity.

items.body:
## What issue are you seeing?

In Codex CLI 0.157.1, a plain left click on a link in the transcript launches a browser on the machine running Codex. I run Codex on an isolated Linux development box over SSH from Konsole on another machine. The browser launch happens on the remote development box, where it is useless, and the click gets in the way of the normal select-and-copy workflow in my local terminal.

Codex reports that it opened or tried to open a browser, so this is Codex handling the click, not Konsole's link handling.

There is no documented setting to disable plain-click link activation while retaining transcript selection. Disabling Konsole's own direct-click link handling does not change Codex's behavior.

## Steps to reproduce

1. SSH to a Linux development machine from Konsole.
2. Run Codex CLI 0.157.1 in its interactive TUI.
3. Have Codex print a Markdown link or bare URL in the transcript.
4. Click the link in the transcript while trying to select or copy it.

The remote Codex process invokes a browser opener. The local Konsole user cannot use that browser, and a stationary click activates the link instead of selecting text.

## Expected behavior

Provide a configuration option to disable Codex's click-to-open behavior (including plain clicks, ideally all Codex-managed link opening) while keeping mouse text selection. For SSH sessions, consider disabling remote browser launch by default, or offering a way to copy the URL instead. Remote detection alone may be unreliable, so an explicit option is important.

## Regression details

PR #46884 (`9fdff739ea0e`, merged 2026-09-20) introduced opening transcript links on unmodified stationary left clicks. The behavior is present in release 0.156.0 and 0.157.0; it is absent from 0.155.0. The relevant code is `codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_view/input.rs`, which returns `ViewAction::OpenLink` on mouse release, and `codex-rs/tui/src/app/history_ui.rs`, which calls `webbrowser::open`.

Workaround: hold Shift while selecting in Konsole so it handles the mouse gesture locally. This is easy to forget and does not provide a persistent Codex setting.

Platform: remote Linux 7.1.8+deb13-amd64 x86_64; local terminal: Konsole over SSH. Codex CLI: 0.157.1.

GPT-6-Sol

### What platform is your computer?

- Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.5 - Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS - Kernel 6.8.0-1065-raspi - AArch64 - Daemon backend: `pid`

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Codex Desktop SSH connection to a remote Linux host

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

After successfully pinning the daemon package from the current CLI, Codex prints this instruction:

```text
The CLI package is selected and pinned. Run `codex app-server daemon update` to return to production updates.
```

However, the suggested command is rejected by the same CLI because `--from-cli` is required:

```text
$ codex app-server daemon update -y
error: the following required arguments were not provided:
  --from-cli

Usage: codex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes
```

As a result, there is no working command matching the CLI's instruction for returning a pinned daemon package to the production update channel.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start with a valid daemon-managed app-server installation.
2. Run:

   ```bash
   codex app-server daemon update --from-cli -y
   ```

3. Observe that the successful result says:

   ```text
   The CLI package is selected and pinned. Run `codex app-server daemon update` to return to production updates.
   ```

4. Follow that instruction by running:

   ```bash
   codex app-server daemon update -y
   ```

5. Observe that argument parsing fails because `--from-cli` is required.

No Codex thread ID is applicable; this reproduces directly in the CLI.

### What is the expected behavior?

One of the following should happen:

- `codex app-server daemon update` is accepted and switches the daemon back to the production update channel; or
- the success message names the actual supported command for leaving the `--from-cli` pinned state.

Instead, the CLI recommends an invocation that its own argument parser rejects.

### Additional information

The daemon itself remained healthy after the rejected command. A subsequent restart succeeded, and `daemon version` reported:

```json
{
  "status": "running",
  "backend": "pid",
  "managedCodexVersion": "0.158.0",
  "cliVersion": "0.158.0",
  "appServerVersion": "0.158.0"
}
```

This appears to be a CLI command/message mismatch rather than a daemon runtime failure.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 25H2
- Codex CLI:
  - Working version: **0.156.1**
  - Broken version: **0.158.0**

## IDE Environment

- IDE: IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3.4 Ultimate Edition
- Build: IU-243.25659.39 (built February 27, 2025)
- Runtime: OpenJDK 21.0.6+8-b631.39 amd64
- JVM: OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM by JetBrains
- Toolkit: sun.awt.windows.WToolkit
- CPU: 16 cores
- Memory: 7680 MB

## Relevant IntelliJ Plugins

- GlassFish: 243.21565.129
- Payara IntelliJ Plugin: 1.12.0
- Java EE EJB support: 243.22562.13
- JSF Plugin: 243.21565.129
- MavenRunHelper: 4.29.0-IJ2022.2
- IntelliJ ML/LLM Plugin: 243.23654.270.9

---

# Problem

After updating Codex CLI from **0.156.1 to 0.158.0**, the Codex panel inside IntelliJ IDEA became unusable.

The problem appears to be related to mouse interaction.

When moving the mouse inside the Codex panel:

- Strange characters are inserted into the Codex output.
- The characters look like terminal escape/control sequences.
- Every mouse movement can generate additional corrupted characters.
- The Codex panel becomes increasingly corrupted and difficult to use.
- Additional Windows Terminal windows opened unexpectedly during the issue.

The problem does **not** occur with Codex CLI **0.156.1** on the same machine and same IntelliJ IDEA installation.

---

# Steps to reproduce

1. Update Codex CLI:

```powershell
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.158.0
```

2. Open IntelliJ IDEA.
3. Open the Codex panel.
4. Start a normal Codex session.
5. Move the mouse inside the Codex panel / terminal area.

Result:
- Terminal-like garbage characters appear immediately.
- Continued mouse movement makes the output corruption worse.

---

# Expected behavior

Mouse movement should have no effect on the Codex text output.

The Codex panel should remain stable and usable.

---

# Actual behavior

Mouse movement appears to send or expose terminal control sequences which are rendered as visible characters in the Codex panel.

The panel becomes corrupted.

---

# Regression information

This is a version regression:

**Same machine:**

✅ Codex CLI 0.156.1  
- Works normally

❌ Codex CLI 0.158.0  
- Mouse movement causes corruption

Rollback command:

```powershell
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.156.1
```

After rollback:

```text
codex-cli 0.156.1
```

The problem disappears immediately.

---

# Additional notes

The issue seems related to terminal mouse handling or escape sequence processing in the IntelliJ integrated environment.

Screenshot attached showing the corrupted Codex panel output.

items.body:
## Summary

Codex CLI `0.158.0` can hang indefinitely before rendering the TUI when running inside tmux if the tmux client selected by Codex's startup probe is incompatible with the active tmux server.

This is a regression from `0.153.4`, which starts successfully in the same environment.

## Environment

- OS: Linux x86_64
- Codex CLI: `0.158.0`
- Active tmux server: `3.1b`, custom installation/socket
- System tmux client: `/usr/bin/tmux` `2.7`
- Interactive shell resolves `tmux` to the matching `3.1b` wrapper before `/usr/bin`

## Reproduction

1. Start or attach to a tmux `3.1b` server using a custom socket.
2. Have tmux `2.7` installed at `/usr/bin/tmux`.
3. Configure the interactive shell's `PATH` so `tmux` resolves to the matching `3.1b` wrapper before `/usr/bin`.
4. Run Codex CLI `0.158.0` inside a tmux pane.

## Actual behavior

Codex hangs before rendering the TUI.

The blocked startup path creates:

```
/usr/bin/tmux display-message -p -t %14 #{extended-keys-format}.#{mouse}
```

The tmux process remains blocked in `poll`, while Codex waits for it to complete.

The Codex parent has the expected user `PATH`, including the custom tmux wrapper. However, the probe child receives a minimal path similar to:

```
/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin
```

As a result, the probe launches `/usr/bin/tmux` rather than the matching `3.1b` client.

## Expected behavior

A tmux capability probe should not be able to block Codex startup indefinitely.

Codex should either:

- resolve `tmux` consistently with the parent environment,
- support explicitly configuring the tmux executable, and/or
- bound the probe with a timeout and continue startup with conservative defaults if it fails.

## Evidence / isolation

The issue can be isolated to the tmux startup probe:

- The capability query returns immediately with the matching tmux `3.1b` client.
- The same query using `/usr/bin/tmux` `2.7` blocks.
- Mapping the matching `3.1b` client over `/usr/bin/tmux` only for the Codex process allows `0.158.0` to start normally.
- Unsetting `TMUX` and `TMUX_PANE` before starting Codex also avoids the hang.
- Codex CLI `0.153.4` starts successfully in the same environment.

## Configuration workarounds tried

The following did not prevent the probe from launching `/usr/bin/tmux`:

```
CODEX_TUI_DISABLE_KEYBOARD_ENHANCEMENT=1
shell_environment_policy.inherit="all"
shell_environment_policy.set.PATH="<custom tmux path>:/usr/bin:/bin"
```

`CODEX_TUI_DISABLE_KEYBOARD_ENHANCEMENT=1` was confirmed present in both the Codex process and the blocked tmux child.

Disabling keyboard enhancement does not eliminate this probe because it also queries tmux mouse state.

## Likely failure path

```
Codex 0.158.0
    |
    +-- detects TMUX / TMUX_PANE
    |
    +-- starts tmux capability probe
            |
            +-- resolves /usr/bin/tmux
            |
            +-- display-message
                    "#{extended-keys-format}.#{mouse}"
            |
            +-- incompatible client/server interaction blocks
                    |
                    +-- Codex waits indefinitely
```

The key robustness issue is not only which tmux executable is selected: an external capability probe can block TUI initialization without a timeout.

## Suggested fix

### 1. Bound the tmux probe

Apply a short timeout to the `tmux display-message` invocation.

If the command fails, cannot connect, or times out, continue startup with conservative capability defaults rather than blocking TUI initialization.

### 2. Fix tmux executable resolution

Resolve `tmux` from the intended parent environment rather than an environment that causes `/usr/bin/tmux` to be selected unexpectedly.

Alternatively, provide a supported configuration option such as:

```
tui.tmux_path = "/path/to/tmux"
```

### 3. Treat capability detection as best-effort

Failure to determine `extended-keys-format` or `mouse` should degrade functionality rather than prevent Codex from starting.

## Regression

| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `0.153.4` | Starts normally |
| `0.158.0` | Hangs before TUI |
| `0.158.0` + matching tmux client | Starts normally |
| `0.158.0` + `TMUX`/`TMUX_PANE` unset | Starts normally |

## Related issue

This appears related to #44767 (Codex CLI 0.154.0 hangs when launched inside tmux), but this report identifies an additional reproducible cause: the startup probe selects an older/incompatible tmux client from a sanitized child `PATH`, and the resulting `display-message` invocation blocks.

### What issue are you seeing?

The archived subagent remains listed in the `/subagents` list after being archived.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Spawn a subagent and let it complete.
2. Run: codex archive <subagent-session-uuid>
3. Confirm the command reports success.
4. Reopen /subagents in the parent session.



### What is the expected behavior?

Archived subagents are hidden by default, or the picker provides
a way to hide completed/archived entries without deleting transcripts
or interrupting other agents.

### Additional information

- The local session record has archived = 1.
- Archiving through the live-session tool also returned success,
  but the entry remained visible.
- The parent–child spawn record still has status "open";
  whether this causes the issue is unknown.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

- Interactive CLI/TUI: `codex-cli 0.157.1`
- Shared background app-server: `codex-cli 0.158.0`
- The turn-end cleanup described below is present in the source for both release tags. A matched 0.158.0 client/server pair has not been tested.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6 Astra, Default mode

### What platform is your computer?

Arch Linux / Omarchy, Wayland: `Linux 7.2.5-3-omarchy x86_64 GNU/Linux`

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Reproduced in foot 1.28.0 and Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2.

### What issue are you seeing?

An unanswered `request_user_input_async` question loses its interactive answer controls when the assistant finishes its turn. The question text can remain in the transcript, while the assistant tells the user to select an option in a question card that is no longer available.

The TUI starts these questions collapsed behind a small question-count indicator. In a minimal Ghostty test, the assistant completed its turn approximately **3.8 seconds** after emitting the question, clearing the pending question before there was a useful opportunity to answer it.

This is a question-UI lifecycle issue; it does not depend on changing terminal emulator or omitting suggested options. The tool's `{"accepted":true}` response acknowledges question submission, not a user answer.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In the Codex CLI, Default mode, ask: **“Use request_user_input_async to ask which color I prefer, with Blue, Green, and Purple as choices. Then tell me to answer the question.”**
2. Do not answer while the assistant is generating its final message.
3. Observe the question indicator/controls during the active turn. The default shortcuts to expand pending questions are Alt+Up or Shift+Left.
4. Let the assistant finish. The pending question controls are cleared, even though no answer was submitted.

The captured test called:

```json
{"questions":[{"title":"Which color do you prefer for this test?","options":["Blue","Green","Purple"]}]}
```

Sanitized rollout evidence, 2026-09-29 UTC:

```text
03:19:26.691  function_call: request_user_input_async
03:19:26.692  item_completed: AgentMessage, delivery="async"
                 questions metadata and all three options present
                 fallback question text present in content[]
                 function_call_output: {"accepted":true}
03:19:30.525  task_complete
```

The final message was: “Select an option in the question card, or type your own answer.” No answer was submitted before completion. TUI logs confirm receipt of the question text and rendering into the transcript.

### What is the expected behavior?

Keep unanswered questions available and answerable after normal turn completion. A completed assistant turn should not silently discard the pending question. Preserve the question until it is answered, explicitly dismissed, or withdrawn. In particular, sending a final message instructing the user to answer should leave the answer controls usable.

### Additional information

Source inspection identifies the cleanup path in `rust-v0.158.0`:

- [Live turn completion calls `take_question_drafts()`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/064c6b8c737f5b41d171fdda80bd9ef10ad06eb3/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/protocol.rs#L457-L459).
- [Recovering drafts calls `clear_pending()`, removing all pending questions](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/064c6b8c737f5b41d171fdda80bd9ef10ad06eb3/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/async_questions/state.rs#L198-L220).
- The existing test [`async_question_notification_expires_when_turn_ends`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/064c6b8c737f5b41d171fdda80bd9ef10ad06eb3/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/tests/question_notifications_tests.rs#L103-L146) explicitly expects zero unanswered questions after a completed, interrupted, or failed turn. Changing this behavior would require updating that expectation.

Related: #43803 reports a similar lifecycle problem in the macOS desktop app; #47535 covers collapsed CLI questions and combined-answer resolution; #48334 involves a queued-message interaction on Windows. This report supplies a Linux CLI reproduction of normal turn-completion cleanup, without queued-message interaction, and the exact source/test path.

items.body:
## Summary

A single brief Ctrl+V in the Codex CLI composer can start a runaway sequence of image-paste attempts. The TUI blocks for roughly 15–18 seconds per attempt, then immediately starts another. The behavior has occurred on this Linux Wayland setup with Codex CLI **0.145.0 and 0.158.0**. It happens both when a screenshot is readable from the clipboard and when no readable image is available. The user now avoids Ctrl+V entirely because the machine became unusable and needed a long power-button press in two 0.158.0 incidents.

This is a dedicated report because the visible effect is repeated paste actions after **one short keypress**, across versions and clipboard states. Related prior report: #27811 (originally a macOS/Warp plain-text paste freeze); my earlier Linux 0.145.0 reproduction and the first 0.158.0 incident were documented in comments there.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.158.0` for the two incidents on 2026-09-29; the older reproduction used `0.145.0`
- Linux aarch64, UKUI Wayland session
- MATE Terminal 1.24.0 / VTE 0.60.3
- External HDMI display at 2560×1440, built-in laptop panel disabled
- `tui.alternate_screen = "never"` at inspection

## Reproduction and comparisons

1. Copy a screenshot to the clipboard, focus the Codex CLI composer, then briefly press Ctrl+V **once** and release it.
2. The composer adds `[Image #1]`, then `[Image #2]`, etc. without further keypresses. Each attachment takes about 15–16 seconds, and the interface remains effectively unusable.
3. Separately, with **no image format readable by Codex** on the clipboard, briefly press Ctrl+V once. Instead of one error, red `Failed to paste image: no image on clipboard ...` messages accumulate continuously, again about every 15–16 seconds. This message does not establish whether the OS clipboard was literally empty or whether its image format was unavailable.
4. As a control, right-click **Paste** with the screenshot in the clipboard produces exactly one `[Image #1]` and works normally on this terminal.

Expected: one image attachment when an image is readable, or one error and an immediate return to an interactive composer when it is not.

## Evidence from `~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`

Local times are UTC+8. Temporary filenames, screenshot contents, and conversation text are omitted.

**Readable screenshot, 2026-09-29:**

```text
10:53:47.803  attempting clipboard image read
10:54:03.503  clipboard image opened: 2560x1440
10:54:03.566  attach_image [temporary PNG #1]
10:54:03.566  attempting clipboard image read
10:54:18.701  attach_image [temporary PNG #2]
10:54:18.701  attempting clipboard image read
...
10:56:25.755  attach_image [temporary PNG #10]
10:56:25.756  attempting clipboard image read [#11]
```

Ten images attached in about 2 minutes 22 seconds; an 11th read had started before shutdown.

**No readable image, separate boot on 2026-09-29:**

```text
11:19:17.973  attempting clipboard image read
11:19:34.121  failed to paste image: no image on clipboard
11:19:34.121  attempting clipboard image read
11:19:49.350  failed to paste image: no image on clipboard
11:19:49.352  attempting clipboard image read
...
11:22:08.842  failed to paste image: no image on clipboard [failure #11]
11:22:08.843  attempting clipboard image read [attempt #12]
```

Each completed attempt is followed within a few milliseconds by another, regardless of success or failure. Kernel logs show a six-second power-button press ending each affected boot; no kernel OOM message was found in either incident window. The precise reason the whole desktop became unusable is unconfirmed.

The prior **0.145.0** Linux reproduction had the same pattern with no readable image: 33 clipboard-read attempts and 32 failures over about 9 minutes 38 seconds on 2026-07-23, with approximately 18 seconds per read ([earlier evidence](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/27811#issuecomment-5056644681)).

The 0.158.0 [Ctrl+V handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/interaction.rs) maps a Ctrl+V `KeyEventKind::Press` to `KeyEventAction::PasteImage`. These logs do not include raw key events, so they cannot identify whether the duplicate actions originate from terminal key-event delivery, Codex input processing, or their interaction. The success/error comparison shows that the repetition is **not limited to an image-read failure path**.

## Requested fix / diagnostic

Please ensure one short Ctrl+V produces at most one paste action, keep the composer responsive while clipboard reads block, and return control after a single failure. Logging the raw key event kind/source when `PasteImage` is dispatched would help locate the duplication. A guard against repeated paste actions while one read is in progress may also prevent runaway attachments/errors.

## Photos of the two visible outcomes

No readable image on the clipboard: repeated red paste errors after one Ctrl+V.

![Codex TUI showing repeated red no-image clipboard errors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/774873df-c261-4fe4-8a3c-d3acf8a16b1a)

Readable screenshot on the clipboard: `[Image #1]` through `[Image #7]` had appeared and more were still being added.

![Codex TUI composer showing seven repeated image placeholders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83910c32-2215-4923-891b-7289c44cc96b)
